question: How do gating topology, pathway overlap, and initialization determine which shared representations win during learning and support zero-shot transfer?

key_findings.claim: Gated Deep Linear Networks reduce a large architecture's gradient-flow dynamics to separate scalar dynamics for singular modes when task covariances and weights share aligned singular vectors.
key_findings.evidence: Path products and context gates yield a compact loss and gradient system; under balanced aligned conditions, each data singular value follows an exact low-dimensional differential equation despite the nonlinear parameter dynamics.

anchors.section: Section 2, Gated Deep Linear Network framework

key_findings.claim: Representations traversed by more tasks learn faster, creating a 'neural race' implicit bias toward maximally shared solutions and enabling untrained input-output routes to generalize once sharing dominates.
key_findings.evidence: The reduced learning rates increase with pathway count P; synthetic routing experiments show fully shared paths dominate alternatives, with transfer emerging when roughly 40% of routes are trained.

key_findings.claim: Small initialization drives rich feature learning and zero-shot transfer, whereas large initialization produces NTK-like lazy dynamics that fit trained routes but preserve separate random representations.
key_findings.evidence: Initialization sweeps show good training across scales but transfer only at small gain; MNIST/CIFAR transformation tasks qualitatively reproduce the approximately 40% sharing threshold, with ten-seed evaluations and a leaky-ReLU relaxation in the appendix.

method.core_idea: Use gated deep linear networks as an exactly reducible proxy for how architecture routes tasks through shared or private parameters.
method.mechanism: Represent active computation as gated graph paths, derive gradient-flow equations from pathwise input-output covariances, impose singular-vector alignment and balance to reduce modes, then vary pathway reuse and initialization to predict representation sharing and transfer.
assumptions: Gates and task routes are supplied rather than learned.
Exact reductions rely on aligned task structure, balanced weights, whitened/orthogonal inputs, and linear layers.
Transformation-based MNIST/CIFAR tasks are meaningful proxies for systematic generalization.

techniques.role: Converts pathwise matrix dynamics into scalar singular-mode equations.
Relates task count through a parameter to its effective learning speed.
Tests representation sharing and transfer across feature-learning and NTK-like regimes.

evaluations.setting: XOR and hierarchical synthetic tasks, then rotated/permuted MNIST and CIFAR input-output route grids with up to 10,000 tasks.
evaluations.metric: Training/untrained-route error, representation similarity, singular-mode trajectories, and error versus initialization gain and trained-route fraction.
evaluations.result: Theory matches simplified dynamics; transfer approaches trained-route performance near 40% route coverage and only under small initialization, with related trends under leaky-ReLU layers.
evaluations.baseline: Private versus partially/fully shared gating and small rich-regime versus large NTK-like initialization.

limitations: Routing/gating is hand-designed, so the theory does not solve architecture or router discovery.
Exact results depend on linearity and strong covariance/singular-vector alignment.
Naturalistic tasks are generated by controlled label/input transformations rather than open-ended compositional benchmarks.
The approximately 40% transition is setup-specific, not a universal constant.
failure_modes: Large initialization locks in private random features and blocks zero-shot transfer despite low training error.
Misaligned task singular spaces break the decoupled scalar dynamics.
Negative transfer occurs when tasks share parameters but not latent structure.
reusable_insights: Parameter reuse changes effective learning speed, not only capacity or compute.
Training error alone cannot distinguish shared feature learning from lazy route memorization.
Architecture studies should jointly vary routing overlap, initialization scale, and held-out task combinations.
open_questions: Can a learned router discover the sharing structure predicted to win the race?
Which parts of the reduction survive in nonlinear transformers or sparse mixture-of-experts models?
Can task similarity predict when sharing produces positive versus negative transfer?

competitive_landscape.title: Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Saxe et al. solve ungated deep-linear singular modes and stage-like learning; the target adds contextual path gates and relates reuse to abstraction and zero-shot task routing.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Lazy-training comparison regime used in the paper.
competitive_landscape.difference: NTK describes infinite-width fixed-feature dynamics; the target emphasizes small-initialization feature movement and shows that lazy fitting can fail systematic transfer.

competitive_landscape.title: Gated Linear Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: GLNs use local convex, backpropagation-free online learners and fixed context gates; GDLNs use backpropagated deep path products as an analytic model of representation sharing.

competitive_landscape.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
competitive_landscape.difference: Sparse MoE learns routing for capacity and compute efficiency at scale; the target derives simplified dynamics explaining when shared versus private routes dominate.

novelty_assessment: The gated deep-linear reduction and pathway-race account are a clear theoretical extension of deep-linear dynamics, connecting architecture reuse to feature learning and systematic transfer. Generalization to learned gates and realistic nonlinear architectures remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated result.
